correctness.rationale: The three-round signature lemma is proved by back-and-forth with equality and explicit definability. For d≥2, N≥8, D≥3, the 00 pattern follows from an edge-count bound ND/2>4D-2; 10/01 from degree and common-neighbor bound; 11 from endpoint incidence. Explicit four-cycle and far-edge witnesses give the uniform stable class and all thin-axis cases. The two smaller graphs (C4 and triangular prism) are exhaustively checked by direct adjacency. One-factor triangular graphs follow from two-set intersections; the displayed nine pointed spectra are pairwise different. Exact direct recursion and orbit-based checks reproduced all nine finite representatives. Finite tests are not used for unbounded quantifiers or parameters.

originality.rationale: Exact statements/implications were compared with accessible earlier Hamming, triangular, and rook-graph theorems and three relevant primary papers. The five one-factor classes are fully credited to the earlier triangular-graph result. Other earlier results concern original Hamming products, coding invariants, embedding properties or unrelated logical signatures and do not entail the nine-class classification after forming line graphs. The rank-three theorem yields genuinely new multi-factor mixed-axis collapse and the sharp 16-edge boundary. The published record could be incomplete and abstract-only papers remain a historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: Line graphs of Hamming products are a natural coding/graph-product family, and forming line graphs changes the first-order domain from words to edges. The classification gives an exact invariant for all dimensions and arbitrary heterogeneous coordinate sizes, isolates two exceptional binary-axis families, proves a cross-dimensional collapse between line graphs of cubes and nonbinary grids, and identifies the sharp minimum representative bound 16. The full parameter result is not a routine corollary of the prior known triangular-graph component.
